issue.title: sase-telegram tests/test_receiver.py is 15/19 red: the service-host guard added by 2f76876 short-circuits ensure_receiver_running in tests
issue.description:
`tests/test_receiver.py` in **sase-telegram** is 15/19 red on a clean tree, because every
`ensure_receiver_running` test now short-circuits before it submits a proc.

`2f76876` (`feat(receiver): register service-host proc`, SASE_BEAD=sase-11y.6) added an
early return to `src/sase_telegram/receiver.py::ensure_receiver_running`:

```python
if _service_host_owns_receiver():
    return None
```

`_service_host_owns_receiver()` reads *ambient* host state — the `service_host` feature
flag plus `sase.service.config.load_service_config()` — neither of which the 15 tests
neutralize. On a host where `service_host` is enabled and the receiver entry is
available, `ensure_receiver_running` returns `None` without ever calling
`submit_proc_request`, so the tests fail as `assert 0 == 1` on `mock_submit.call_count`
or `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'proc_id'`.

Reproduced 2026-09-20 in the sase_10 linked sase-telegram checkout at master `4d20559`
(clean tree, `just install`), against sase at both `6087c0a8e` and `598f1e820`:
`15 failed, 4 passed in 1.71s`. Deterministic across both sase versions and re-runs —
not intermittent, and not a flake: the guard fires on every call.

Failing nodes (15): `TestEnsureReceiverRunning::test_submits_a_deterministic_request`,
`::test_two_calls_carry_the_same_fingerprint_and_concurrency_key`,
`::test_recent_launch_failure_notifies_once_and_suppresses_rearm`,
`::test_absent_or_healthy_newest_row_rearms[None|row1|row2|row3]`,
`::test_old_launch_failure_rearms_after_backoff`;
`TestReceiverLaunchFailureNotifications::test_recent_launch_failure_creates_real_notification_during_backoff`,
`::test_existing_notification_blocks_repeated_ticks_even_when_dismissed[False|True]`,
`::test_expired_launch_failure_notifies_and_rearms_with_real_store`,
`::test_stale_empty_snapshot_race_plus_ones_existing_notification`;
`TestSingleOwnerReplay::test_second_ensure_call_replays_the_first`,
`::test_ensure_after_termination_launches_a_fresh_receiver`.

The likely fix is to make the tests hermetic with respect to the service-host guard
(force `_service_host_owns_receiver` to `False`, or isolate the flag and service config
the same way `sandbox_home` isolates `SASE_HOME`) and to add one test that covers the
service-host-owned branch deliberately. Decide whether the guard's dependence on ambient
host config is itself correct: today the same call behaves differently on two developer
machines.

Found by the `sase-zr.7` land agent while disposing of the `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP:` note on
phase bead `sase-zr.7.5` (note #1), which first observed these 15 failures on 2026-09-20.
Not caused by epic `sase-zr`: the epic's only sase-telegram commits are `24900c0`
(sase-zr.7.4, inbound auth) and `4d20559` (sase-zr.7.5, docs), and the full suite passed
at 636 tests when `24900c0` landed on 2026-09-16.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: _service_host_owns_receiver() reads the ambient service_host flag and service config, which the tests never neutralize, so ensure_receiver_running returns None on every call. 15 failed / 4 passed reproduced on a clean tree against sase 6087c0a8e and 598f1e820, and again on re-run.
